findings.failure_scenario: `crewai tools publish` in any valid tool project: extract_available_exports() returns e.g. [{"name": "MyTool"}] (src/crewai/cli/utils.py:409-415) and SystemExits when empty, so the `if available_exports:` guard is always truthy when reached; `', '.join(...)` then raises TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, dict found, aborting publish before the tarball is built. The tests miss it because test_main.py mocks extract_available_exports with return_value=["SampleTool"] (strings). The same dict values would also be sent to publish_tool, whose parameter is typed Optional[List[str]].
findings.summary: `', '.join(available_exports)` crashes because extract_available_exports returns a list of dicts ({"name": ...}), not strings

findings.failure_scenario: `crewai tools create my-tool` scaffolds src/my_tool/__init__.py containing `from .tool import MyTool` (the new template at src/crewai/cli/templates/tool/src/{{folder_name}}/__init__.py:1). On `crewai tools publish`, _load_tools_from_init calls spec_from_file_location("temp_module", <init file>) — the name has no dot and no submodule_search_locations is passed, so the module's __package__ ends up '' (or its __path__ is empty), making the relative import raise ImportError ('attempted relative import with no known parent package' / ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'temp_module.tool'). The except at line 417 catches it and raises SystemExit(1): publishing is impossible for every project created from the new template. All tests use absolute imports, so this path is untested.
findings.summary: Every __init__.py is exec'd as a bare top-level module named 'temp_module', so the relative import shipped in the new tool template cannot resolve

findings.failure_scenario: The old tool template shipped an empty src/<folder>/__init__.py (the diff's index e69de29 is the empty-file blob), and any project may contain packages without __all__ (e.g. src/config/__init__.py). After this change, `crewai tools publish` on such a project loads the init file, finds no __all__ attribute, prints the warning and raises SystemExit(1) at line 407 — the command that previously worked unconditionally now exits with code 1 for all pre-existing tool projects. There is no migration path: the user must hand-edit every __init__.py to add __all__.
findings.summary: Publish now hard-aborts (SystemExit) when any scanned __init__.py lacks __all__, breaking every tool project created with the previous CLI

findings.failure_scenario: A PR touching only e.g. src/crewai/cli/templates/tool/src/{{folder_name}}/tool.py passes the `files != ''` guard, but after `grep -v 'src/crewai/cli/templates/'` the pipeline is empty: grep exits 1, which fails the step under GitHub Actions' default `bash -eo pipefail`, and `xargs -I{}` without `-r` additionally runs `ruff check ""` once on empty input, exiting non-zero. Either way the lint job goes red for exactly the template-only changes the filter was added to permit.
findings.summary: The grep -v template filter fails the lint step on PRs whose changed .py files are all templates

findings.failure_scenario: A user's __init__.py that exports a class inheriting from a different library's BaseTool — e.g. `from langchain_core.tools import BaseTool; class MyLCTool(BaseTool): ...; __all__ = ['MyLCTool']` — passes the getmro name check because langchain's base class is also named 'BaseTool', so the class is reported in available_exports and published as a CrewAI tool export. The check should be `issubclass(obj, BaseTool)` (the crewai BaseTool is already importable alongside Tool at line 347); the name-based check also accepts crewai's own abstract BaseTool if re-exported.
findings.summary: is_valid_tool matches any MRO member whose __name__ is 'BaseTool' instead of crewai's BaseTool by identity, accepting unrelated classes as valid tools
